description_en: The temple of Karuṇāmaya is one of the rare Śikhara-style Buddhist temples in the Valley. Karuṇāmaya is however but one of the names that the deity enshrined within goes by; he is also referred to as Buṅgadyaḥ, Rāto Matsyendranātha, Lokanātha, Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara, Avalokiteśvara, Āryāvalokiteśvara, etc. The deity is worshipped as the god of rain and plenty. He is considered to be Lokeśvara by Buddhists, Matsyendranātha by Śaivas and Viriñcinārāyaṇa by Vaiṣṇavas. Sundarānanda, an early 19th-century poet from Patan, calls the deity Matsyendranātha and explains that Vaiṣṇavas call him Viṣṇu, Śaivas call him Śiva, Śāktas know him as Śakti, Brahmins think of him as Brahmā, hermits call him Matsyendra, Buddhists call him Lokeśvara, and others call him Bhāskara (Triratnasaundaryagāthā73).No historical records could be traced that confirm the initial construction date of the temple.Gutschow(2011, 534) assumes that the temple once had three terracotta-tiled roofs but that the structure collapsed on 26 August 1833 when the Kathmandu Valley was hit by a disastrous earthquake. He suggests that the 17th-century inner cella and its four original doors were preserved. The outer arcade was reconstructed using new large stone pillars and a heavy timber frame, whilst the upper structure was rebuilt in the shape of a Śikhara temple rather than in its original three-tiered configuration. The temple suffered only minor damage in the great earthquake of 1934 (Locke1980, 324) but collapsed in the 2015 earthquake. As of November 2019 it is under reconstruction.Along with the procession of Karuṇāmaya, which starts on the first day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, many festivals, worships and rituals began here. There are also manyguṭhīsrelated to the deity and the temple. A Bungamati group of thirty-onepānejus(priests) plays a vital role in organising processions and other worships related to the deity.Bungamati is one of the oldest settlements in the Kathmandu Valley. The two Licchavi inscriptions that have been found in the village do not make any mention Karuṇāmaya Mandira. The first inscription refers to the village as 'Bugāyumīgrāma' (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2030, 290). The second one has been badly damaged, but appears to speak of someone who will have mercy on living beings (Ibid. 586-87).Locke(1980, 250) assumes that this inscription refers to Karuṇāmaya (lit. "The one who is full of compassion"). One of the inscriptions placed at the temple of the same deity in Taḥ Bāhāḥ, Patan (LAL0050) mentions that King Śrīnivāsa Malla made many provisions for the cult of the deity in 1673 (Locke1980, 308). During medieval times, coins bearing Buṅgdyaḥ's name were issued (H. Śākya,VS 2048, 16) and postage stamps are now available with his image.Many of the Nepalese chronicles tell the story of King Narendradeva bringing Matsyendranātha from Kāmarū-Kāmākṣa or Kāmarūparvata to Nepal. TheGopālarājavaṁśāvalī(1985, fol. 23a) mentions that King Narendradeva and Acharya Bandhudatta began the procession of Bugmalokeśvara. However, as three kings with the name Narendradeva ruled over Nepal in different periods (Slusser1982, vol. 1, 397-398), the question arises as to which king first started the procession. Most scholars agree that it was the first Narendradeva (643-679 CE). According toK. Tamoṭa(NS 1129, 63), a manuscript preserved in the National Archives of Nepal mentions that Narendradeva brought Buṅgadyaḥ to Nepal 305 years before the beginning of Nepal Saṃvat, which started in 879 CE. A number of inscriptions were also placed by King Narendradeva I; none of them, however, mentions the deity. TheNepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī(13.68-76) records the legend that Āryāvalokiteśvara Padmapāṇi Bodhisattva, disguised as a fish (matsya), was listening whilst Lord Śiva was taught Pārvatī yoga. Thereafter, Bodhisattva was known as Matsyendranātha. The chronicle further tells how King Narendradeva andācāryaBandhudatta brought Matsyendranātha to Nepa, made his shrine in Bungmati and began the tradition of the Bugmalokeśvara procession.
description_ne: उपत्यकाका प्राचीन बस्तीहरूमध्ये बुङ्गमती पनि एक हो । सन् ६०५ को अंशुवर्माको अभिलेखमा बुङ्गमतीलाई 'बुगायूमी' भनिएको छ (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2030, 290) । ठाउँकै नामको आधारमा अर्थात् बुङ्गमतीका देवता भन्ने अर्थमा यस करुणामयलाई बुङ्गमती एवं पाटनका नेवार समुदायले 'बुङ्गद्यः' भन्दै आएका छन् । यसको विपरीत बुङ्गद्यःको वास भएको ठाउँ भएबाट ठाउँको नाम बुङ्गमती रहन गएको हो भनी व्याख्या गर्नेहरू पनि भेटिन्छन् (T. Siṃha, VS 2075, 78) ।  बुङ्गद्यः र करुणामयको अलावा उनलाई रातो मच्छिन्द्रनाथ, लोकनाथ, पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वर, अवलोकितेश्वर, आर्यावलोकितेश्वर  जस्ता अनेक नामले पुकारिएको पाइन्छ । राजा नरेन्द्रदेवले भारतको कामारुकामाक्षा (वर्तमान आसाम)बाट बुङ्गद्यःलाई नेपाल ल्याएको लोककथा उपत्यकामा नेवार समुदायमाझ  प्रसिद्ध छ । वंशावलीहरूमा यस कथाको उल्लेख पाइन्छ । कथाको मूलसार एउटै भए तापनि कथाका पात्र एवं घटनाहरूमा भने  वंशावली पिच्छे केही भेद भएको पाइन्छ। विभिन्न वंशावलीहरूले बुङ्गद्यः ल्याइएको कुरा व्याख्या गर्दे कलिगत संवत्मा भिन्ना भिन्नै मिति प्रस्तुत गरेका छन् । इतिहास अध्ययन क्षेत्रमा विश्वसनीय मानिएको गोपालराज वंशावलीमा भने राजा नरेन्द्रदेव र आचार्य बन्धुदत्त मिली बुङ्गद्यःको जात्रा चलाए भनी लेखिएको छ (Gopālarājavaṁśāvalī, 1985, पत्र २३ क) । नेपालको इतिहासमा ७ औं देखि १२ औं शताब्दीभित्रमा नरेन्द्रदेव नाम गरेका तीन राजाहरू पाइएका छन् (Locke1973, 39) । ती तीनमध्ये ७ औं शदीका लिच्छवि राजा नरेन्द्रदेवले नै बुङ्गद्यःको जात्रा चलाएको भनी तर्क गर्नेहरूको संख्या बढी छ । राष्ट्रिय अभिलेखालयमा सुरक्षित एक थ्यासफूमा पनि नरेन्द्रदेवले नेपाल संवत् शुरु हुनु भन्दा ३०५ वर्ष पूर्व बुङ्गद्यः नेपाल ल्याएको घटना टिपोट गरिएको छ (K. Tamoṭa, NS 1129, 61) । यसरी हेर्दा लिच्छवि राजा नरेन्द्रदेवको पालामा बुङ्गद्यः ल्याइएको कुरा बढी विश्वसनीय हुन आए पनि स्वंय नरेन्द्रदेवले राख्न लगाएका कुनै पनि अभिलेखमा बुङ्गद्यः वा लोकेश्वरलाई जनाउने कुनै शब्दसम्म पनि उल्लेख भएको पाइदैन । स्लसरले (Slusser1982, vol. 2, plate no. 594 and 595 मा) बुङ्गद्यःको चित्र भएका दुईवटा हस्तलिखित ग्रन्थको गाताको केही अंश प्रकाशित गरेकी छिन् र त्यो मध्ये पहिलोलाई सन् १०७१ भनेकी छिन् । तर सो ग्रन्थको लिपि हेर्दा त्यो ग्रन्थ १०७१ को नभएर १६ औं १७ औं शताब्दीतिरको जस्तो देखिन्छ ।उपत्यकामा कमै मात्र पाइने शिखर शैलीका बौद्ध मन्दिरहरूमध्येमा यो पनि पर्दछ । यस मन्दिरको निर्माण मिति एवं निर्माताबारे जानकारी पाउन सकिने विश्वसनीय आधार पाइएको छैन । अधिकांश विद्वान्हरू निकै अघि नै बुङ्गमतीमा बुङ्गद्यःको मन्दिर बनेको हुनुपर्ने विचार व्यक्त गर्छन् । तर मन्दिरको ऐतिहासिकतालाई निक्र्यौल गर्ने बलियो स्रोतको अभाव छ । मन्दिर शुरुदेखि नै शिखर शैलीमा निर्मित थियो वा पछि मात्र यो शैलीमा पुनःनिर्माण गरिएको हो भन्ने कुराको पनि निश्चय भैसकेको छैन । सन् १८३४ को भूकम्पले ठुलो क्षति पुगेको मन्दिर सन् १९३४ को भूकम्पमा भने पूर्ण रूपले भत्किएको थियो । फेरि सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पमा मन्दिर भत्किएपछि हाल पुनःनिर्माणको चरणमा रहेको छ ।यस मन्दिरको गर्भगृहमा बुङ्गद्यःको मूर्ति ६ महिना राखिन्छ भने बाँकी ६ महिना पाटनको तःबहामा रहेको तल्ले शैलीको मन्दिरमा (LAL0060) राख्ने परम्परा छ । यसरी दुई ठुला–ठुला मन्दिर भएका अन्य कुनै देव–देवी उपत्यकामा पाइदैन। दुई मन्दिरको गर्भगृहका साथै वर्षेनी रथमा राखिने बुङ्गद्यःको मूर्ति करिब ४ फीट अग्लो छ (M. Vajrācārya,2002, 8) । शुभश्री मित्रले बुङ्गद्यःको मूर्ति करुणाचुक बहीमा (LAL1560) बनाएको जनधारणा रहेको छ  (Ā. Vajrācārya,1985: 84 )। करुणामयको मूर्ति बनाइएको बही भएबाट बहीको नाम करुणाचुक रहन गएको भनाई पाइन्छ । सन् १२२६ देखि १२३४ सम्म नेपालमा बसेका धर्मस्वामीले भारतसम्म प्रख्यात भएका र शरद् ऋतुमा जात्रा मनाइने बुङ्गद्यःको मूर्ति ५ फीट अग्लो हुनेगरी चन्दनको काँठबाट बनाइएको उल्लेख गरेका छन् (Regmī1965, 560) । बुङ्गद्यःको मुखाकृति माटोबाट र अन्यभाग धातुबाट बनेको छ । माटोबाट बनेको मुखको भागलाई वर्षेनी बुङ्गमतीबाट पाटनको तःबाहाःमा ल्याउँदा  र रथजात्रा गरिनु पूर्व नयाँ बनाई रङ्गरोदन गर्ने चलन छ ।सहकालका देवता मानिने बुङ्गद्यःलाई शैव मार्गीले नाथ र बौद्ध मार्गीले लोकेश्वर मान्दै आएका छन् । त्यसैगरी उनलाई वैष्णव देवका रूपमा विरञ्चिनारायण भनिएको प्रमाण पनि पाइन्छन्  (J.Mānandhara,VS 2046, 116) । यसरी विभिन्न सम्प्रदायबाट आस्थापूर्वक पूजिने वुङ्गद्यः प्राचीनकालदेखि नै उपत्यकामा निकै प्रसिद्ध देवमध्येका एक हुन् । उत्तर मध्यकालमा बुङ्गद्यःको नाम उल्लेख गरी विभिन्न राजाहरूबाट मुद्रा निस्कासन भएको पाइन्छ (H. Śākya,VS 2048, 16) । हाल पनि बुङ्गद्यः राजकीय मान्यता प्राप्त देवमध्येका एक हुन् । उनको चित्र अंकित हुलाक टिकट पनि प्रकाशित छ । प्राचीनकालदेखि प्रसिद्धि पाउँदै आएका बुङ्गद्यःको रथजात्रा पनि उतिकै प्रख्यात छ । जात्राका साथै वार्षिक रूपमा सम्पन्न गरिने बुङ्गद्यःसँग सम्बिन्धित अनेकन पूजा, पर्व, होम एवं अनुष्ठानहरू रहेका छन् । यी सांस्कृतिक कर्महरू नियमित संचालन गर्ने अनेकन गुठीहरू अस्तित्वमा छन् । बुङ्गमतीका ३१ पानेजु समूहले बुङ्गद्यःसँग सम्बन्धित अमूर्त संस्कृति संचालनमा अहम् भूमिका निर्वाह गर्दै आएका छन् ।

historical_events.event_name: Levelling the temple
historical_events.event_description: The temple was levelled in the 1934 earthquake.

historical_events.event_name: Reconstruction
historical_events.event_description: As of November 2019 the temple is under reconstruction. The project is managed by the Department of Archaology, Nepal with funding from the Embassy of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka.

historical_events.event_name: A week-long event of reciting the texts and hymns
historical_events.event_description: Guru Kavi Prasada organisedsaptāhakīrtana(a one-week long religious event) in Bungmati.

historical_events.event_name: Formation of a guṭhī in 1662 CE
historical_events.event_description: In 1662, King Śrīnivāsa Malla set up aguṭhīto run theāratī pūjāin the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of an inscription containing the regulations to govern the cultural events and activities
historical_events.event_description: Śrīnivāsa Malla installed a long inscription at the temple at Taḥ Bāhāḥ (LAL0050), which provides regulations to govern the cultural events and activities of Karuṇāmaya. The King of Patan must take personal responsibility for the arrangements for the bathing ceremony, the chariot procession and Karuṇāmaya's journey to Patan (Locke1980, 309).

historical_events.event_name: Installation of an inscription regulating the Kārttika fesitval
historical_events.event_description: Śrīnivāsa Malla installed an inscription at the temple to regulate the Kārttika festival. The inscription states that women of the Dhobi (washermen), Jogī (Kusle) and Kasāi (butcher) caste are not allowed to take the vow (vrata) to participate in the festival. Only those who come on the full moon day (24 hours) of Āśvina are allowed to take thevrata. The king had also endowed land to feed the devotees at the end of the festival.

historical_events.event_name: Formation of a guṭhī by King Śrīnivāsa Malla in 1672 CE
historical_events.event_description: King Śrīnivāsa Malla set up aguṭhīforāratī pūjāin the Karuṇāmaya temple at Bungmati.Nepālako Itihāsa Rājabhogamālā(inAncient Nepal10, p. 5) mentions that this took place in NS 702.

historical_events.event_name: Pavement of the courtyard with black stone
historical_events.event_description: The temple courtyard was paved with black stone.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of golden toraṇa by a minister of King Jayasthiti Malla
historical_events.event_description: An inscription from Ituṃ Bahāla mentions that a minister of King Jayasthiti Malla, Madanarāmavarddhana (brother of Jayasiṃharāmavarddhana) and his wife Jaitralakṣmī offered a goldentoraṇato Buṅgmalokeśvara.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a crown to Bugmalokeśvara by King Bālārjunadeva
historical_events.event_description: King Bālārjunadeva offered his crown to Bugmalokeśvara. TheGopālarājavaṃśāvalī(fol. 23a) mentions this event.

historical_events.event_name: Donation by King Ripu Malla
historical_events.event_description: Gopālarājavaṃśāvalī(fol. 43a) mentions that King Ripu Malla, the King of Khasāna, anointed the Buṅga deity and donated treasures.

historical_events.event_name: Participation of king Jayasthiti Malla in Buṅgadyaḥ's procession
historical_events.event_description: King Jayasthiti Malla went to Bugma Jātrā with his three sons.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a silver chain by King Mukunda Sen
historical_events.event_description: King Mukunda Sen from Palpa came to the chariot procession of Buṅgadyaḥ and offered a silver chain to the deity.

historical_events.event_name: A land endowment to establish a guṭhī for the bathing ceremony of Buṅgadyaḥ and Ādinātha (of Chobhar)
historical_events.event_description: A copper-plate inscription preserved in the National Archives and dated NS 678 states that Melvagha Varma, Hṛdayasiṃha Varma, Jñānasiṃha Varma and Keśavasiṃha Varma from Jyeṣṭhavarṇa Vihāra Patan granted land to establish aguṭhīfor the bathing ceremony of Buṅgadyaḥ and Ādinātha (of Chobhar).

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of a guṭhī for organising hāthuhāyukegu (see below)
historical_events.event_description: King Jayanarasiṃha established aguṭhīto organisehāthuhāyukeguduring the chariot procession of Karuṇāmaya.Hāthuhāyekeguis a tradition of placing a mud vessel filled with local liquor (chyāṅ) behind the mask of Bhairava and connecting a pipe to his mouth from which the liquor comes. People drink the liquor during the chariot procession.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a water vessel by King Viṣṇu Malla
historical_events.event_description: After thenhvã(bathing) of Buṅgadyaḥ in the sanctum of the temple, a water vessel called Brahmakvã is placed in the sanctum of the temple for one week. King Viṣṇu Malla offered a Brahmakvã to the deity.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a parasol and four banners by King Rājyaprakāśa Malla
historical_events.event_description: King Rājyaprakāśa Malla offered akhatajalā(?), a parasol and four banners to the deity.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of gold by a king of Sikkim
historical_events.event_description: Paṇḍita Jīvarāja and Jayamuni from Gāḥ Bāhāḥ (LAL0510) went to Sikkim and offered a full plateprasāda(gift) to the King of Sikkim. In gratitude, the King filled the plate with gold. When Jayamuni returned with the gold, he called a meeting of the members of thesaṅghato decide what to do with it. They decided to make fixtures (side panels for the four sides, thetoraṇas, and the decorations above thetoraṇasfor the chariot) for the Red Matsyendranātha. The fixtures were placed on the chariot for the first time in NS 774 after the chariot arrived at Gāḥ Bāhāḥ. Aguṭhīknown as theLusa Guṭhīwas then set up to ensure the safekeeping and maintenance of the fixtures.

historical_events.event_name: Coins minted under the name of Buṅgadyaḥ

historical_events.event_name: Pavement of steps in front of the outer entrance of the temple
historical_events.event_description: The steps in front of the outer entrance of the temple were paved with stones. The steps around the stone lions were also paved.

historical_events.event_name: References to Bugmalokeśvara (Buṅgadyaḥ) in the palm-leaf manuscripts
historical_events.event_description: Slusser(1982, vol. 2, plate no. 594 and 595) gives photos of two Nepalese manuscripts with depictions of Bugmalokeśvara. She dates the first manuscript to 1071 CE and the second to 1679 CE. However, she does not provide any further details regarding the manuscripts and does not mention anything about how she dated them. Paleographically, the first manuscript cannot be from such an early date. It is more likely that it comes from the 17th-18th century.Locke(1980, 300) also mentions one such manuscript containing a miniture painting of Bugama Lokeśvara preserved in Paris and vaguely dates it to 120-220 NS.

historical_events.event_name: Erection of a stone pillar
historical_events.event_description: A stone pillar with a statue of Vajrasatva was erected in front of the Karuṇāmaya temple.

historical_events.event_name: Damage from the 1834 earthquakes
historical_events.event_description: The monument was seriously damaged in the 1834 earthquakes.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a bell
historical_events.event_description: Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura Kũvara Rāṇā offered a bell to Buṅgadyaḥ.
